title: Model Provenance & IP Indemnity Schedule
content:
Purpose:
This schedule supplements the Agreement between the Parties and sets forth (a) the Supplier's obligations to maintain and hand over model provenance and evidence of origin for any model weights, training or pretraining datasets, and third-party components provided to the Customer, and (b) the Supplier's limited IP indemnity commitments related to those models.

Scope and Applicability:
- Applies to all Model Deliverables defined in the Agreement ("Model") and any associated artifacts the Supplier provides to Customer for production serving, testing, or deployment.
- Does not modify obligations for open-source components except where expressly stated in section "Open Source and License Evidence" below.

Definitions (selected):
- "Provenance Records": persistent records demonstrating origin, chain-of-custody, and handling of model artifacts, including but not limited to hashes, manifests, signed attestations, training-data lineage reports, and third-party license receipts.
- "Model Deliverable": trained model weights, configuration, tokenizers, and any additional artifacts the Supplier supplies to Customer.
- "Third-Party Component": any software, weights, model checkpoint, dataset, or tool not authored solely by Supplier (including open-source and commercial elements).

Supplier Obligations: Provenance and Evidence
1) Provenance Records. For each Model Deliverable, Supplier will maintain and provide to Customer upon request:
   a) a cryptographic hash of the model weights and an accompanying manifest specifying origin, training snapshot id, and generation date;
   b) a signed attestation (PGP or equivalent) from the engineering owner that the manifest matches the delivered artifact;
   c) a dataset lineage summary showing the categories of data sources used for pretraining and fine-tuning (P–II redacted as required), with references to internal dataset IDs;
   d) a list of all Third-Party Components and a copy of the corresponding license or commercial agreement;
   e) a short technical note describing any post-processing, pruning, or quantization applied to the weights after training.

2) Chain-of-Custody Logs. Supplier will retain an immutable audit trail showing transfers, transformations, and access to the Model Deliverable (including CI/CD artifacts, storage locations, and personnel or service accounts with access) for the Retention Period.

3) Retention Period. Supplier will retain Provenance Records and Chain-of-Custody Logs for a minimum of three (3) years from delivery or for such longer period as required by applicable law or the Agreement.

4) Secure Storage & Access Controls. Provenance Records must be stored with integrity protections (signed manifests, tamper-evident logs) and access controls consistent with Supplier's SOC 2 / ISO practices described in the Agreement.

Open Source and License Evidence
- For any Third-Party Component released under an open-source license, Supplier will provide: (i) the exact version identifier (commit/tag) used; (ii) the license text; and (iii) a short compatibility note if such component imposes requirements on redistribution or attribution.
- If a license condition would impose obligations on Customer that are inconsistent with the Agreement (e.g., copyleft obligations that affect Customer's closed-source services), Supplier will (at Supplier's option) either: (A) remediate by replacing the component with a compatible alternative free of the incompatible condition; or (B) notify Customer in writing and propose a mitigation plan.

IP Indemnity (Model-Specific Narrow Indemnity)
1) Supplier Indemnity Scope. Subject to the limitations and exclusions below, Supplier will indemnify, defend and hold harmless Customer from Losses resulting from any third-party claim that the Model Deliverable, as delivered by Supplier and used in accordance with the Agreement, infringes or misappropriates a third party's issued patents, copyrights, or trade secrets.

2) Conditions. The indemnity applies only where Customer: (a) uses the Model Deliverable without modification or only with modifications expressly approved in writing by Supplier; (b) promptly notifies Supplier in writing of the claim; and (c) gives Supplier sole control of the defense and settlement of the claim.

3) Exclusions. The indemnity will not apply to claims arising from:
   a) Customer's combination of the Model with third-party software or data not provided or authorized by Supplier where the alleged infringement is caused by that combination;
   b) modifications by Customer or any third party that alter the Model's behavior in a way that gives rise to the claim;
   c) use outside the licensed scope (e.g., commercial redistribution if only an evaluation license was granted);
   d) open-source components where the claim arises solely from the terms of that open-source license and Supplier provided appropriate license evidence as required above.

4) Remedies. If a claim is made or likely, Supplier may at its option and expense: (i) procure the right for Customer to continue using the Model; (ii) replace or modify the Model to be non-infringing with substantially equivalent performance; or (iii) if neither (i) nor (ii) is commercially practicable, terminate the license for the affected Model and refund any prepaid fees covering the unused portion of the term.

5) Financial Cap. The Supplier's indemnity obligations under this Schedule are subject to the liability cap in the Agreement but in no event shall exceed the indemnity cap set forth in the Agreement for third-party IP claims.

Notice, Defense, and Cooperation
- Customer will provide prompt written notice of any claim and cooperate reasonably in the defense. Supplier will not settle any claim that imposes a liability or obligation on Customer without Customer's prior written consent (which shall not be unreasonably withheld).

Audit & Inspection Rights
1) Right to Evidence. Upon reasonable notice and subject to confidentiality protections and operational constraints, Customer may request copies of Provenance Records and redacted Chain-of-Custody Logs for a reasonable subset of Model Deliverables once per calendar year.
2) On-site or Remote Audit. If Customer reasonably suspects material non-compliance with this Schedule, Customer may request an audit. Parties will use commercially reasonable efforts to conduct remote evidence exchanges first. On-site audits will be scoped, scheduled, and limited to minimize operational disruption; Supplier may require a protective order or an NDA to protect internal details.
3) Cost Allocation. If an audit reveals material non-compliance, Supplier will reimburse Customer for reasonable incremental costs of the audit. If no material non-compliance is found, Customer will reimburse Supplier for Supplier's reasonable costs incurred in supporting the audit.

Transition Assistance and Deliverables on Termination
- Upon termination or expiration of the Agreement, Supplier will, for a period of thirty (30) days, provide Customer with a copy of the Provenance Records, manifests, hashes, and a best-effort checklist for rehosting the Model Deliverable in Customer's environment (subject to existing license terms). Extended transition support may be mutually agreed and charged per the Agreement.

Confidentiality and Redaction
- Supplier may redact personally identifiable information (PII) or proprietary operational details from Provenance Records to the extent necessary, but redactions must be identified and an unredacted version must be made available for review under appropriate protective arrangements (e.g., in a secure room or under a protective order).

Limitations & Carveouts
- This Schedule does not convert Supplier's general warranties or representations into broader indemnity obligations beyond the IP scope described herein. Supplier is not a guarantor of downstream classifiers, outputs, or application-layer decisions made by Customer.

Amendment, Governing Law, and Execution
- Any amendment to this Schedule must be in writing and signed by authorized representatives.
- This Schedule is governed by the governing law and dispute resolution provisions set forth in the Agreement.

Operational Notes (internal guidance for implementation):
- Engineering to produce a standard Provenance Manifest template (Confluence: PROV-2024).
- Security to validate storage and signing approach during quarterly audit windows (JIRA-SEC-988).
- Legal to review and approve customer-facing indemnity language for commercial negotiations; if Customer requests broader IP indemnity, escalate to Head of Legal.
